key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer formed during CuInSe2 growth can passivate the back contact and enable high-voltage 1.0 eV bottom cells without heavy-alkali or Ag additions.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact engineering route for tandem-ready CuInSe2 absorbers, helping push efficiency above 16% while maintaining a record VOC above 550 mV.
method: Formed GaOx by ion exchange during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap absorber.
Tested whether extra Cu, Na, or sputtering oxygen flow controls GaOx conductivity.
Used device optimization to correlate GaOx structure with solar-cell performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an optimized active-area device efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV.
watch_item: The conductive GaOx appears sensitive to formation conditions and partial crystallinity, so reproducibility and back-contact compatibility need careful process control.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
